messages:
Nora (PM): Quick thread — roadmap call flagged billing/quotas as the biggest blocker for Dedicated customers. Need a decision on committed tiers vs burst credits by EOW.

Aisha Khan: Agreed. Customers want predictable spend. We should support: reserved qps, burst credits, per-token billing for hosted, and an overage grace window.

Mike Chen: If we give deep committed discounts we risk underutilization and abuse. Suggest auto-rollover credits for unused commit into the next billing period (opt-in).

Priya Nair: Regulatory customers can't accept rollovers without explicit contract language. They also prefer hard caps with negotiated overage rates.

Jared Lee: Drafting a simple policy: three commitment tiers (dev/prod/enterprise). Burst pool lives on top of reserved capacity and is limited by tokens/sec and daily quota. Example policy: 

```json
{
  "tier": "prod",
  "reserved_tokens_per_min": 50000,
  "burst_pool_tokens": 20000,
  "burst_window_sec": 60,
  "overage_rate_per_1k_tokens": "0.008",
  "grace_window_days": 3
}
```

billing-bot: FYI — last experiment with 30–40% discounts showed ~12% negative margin when churn hit 20%. Keep discounting conservative.

Aisha Khan: Launch criteria proposal: public docs + UI for selecting commit, backend meters & telemetry per-tenant, billing integration tests, and a rollback path to hosted pay-as-you-go.

Nora (PM): Prioritization: push this into Q2 spike — 2 sprints to validate backend + UI + billing hooks. Top enterprise trials should be migrated in Q3.

Mike Chen: Engineering question: how do we define "burst" precisely — tokens/sec, qps, or both? I vote tokens/sec because token usage better reflects cost.

Priya Nair: Legal ask: explicit opt-in for auto-rollover and auto-renewal. Also require cap on chargebacks for disputed overages. Flagged for contract review.

Jared Lee: Rollout plan: canary with 2 customers on isolated capacity, monitor cost delta and QoS for 2 weeks, then 10% user slice, then full. Automatic fallback to pay-as-you-go if SLA or cost thresholds breached.

Aisha Khan: @sales-team I'll spin up a one-pager for enterprise negotiation playbook (negotiable discounts, minimum commitments, churn protections).

Nora (PM): Action items: Aisha — spec + one-pager by Thu; Mike — estimate story points and implementation risks; Priya — legal hooks & contract language; Jared — canary run plan + metric dashboard. I'll schedule a sync Fri morning.

Mike Chen: Quick note — we should surface a simulated invoice preview in the UI so customers can see commit vs burst vs overage costs before they sign.

Priya Nair: +1 on invoice preview. Also add an explicit checkbox for "no-rollover" for regulated customers.

Nora (PM): Great. If no objections, I'll convert these into GH tickets and add to the roadmap board. :thumbsup:
